content.front: True or false? Adding a data destination to a Dataflow Gen2 is mandatory — a dataflow cannot exist without one.
content.back: False. A data destination is explicitly described as optional — the dataflow preserves all transformation steps regardless, and can be incorporated into a pipeline for further use without a destination set. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-dataflow-gen-2-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Dataflows Gen2 can be used as a reusable, discoverable data source that data analysts connect to directly from Power BI Desktop.
content.back: True. Making a dataflow discoverable lets analysts connect to it via Power BI Desktop, reducing data prep duplication for report development. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-dataflow-gen-2-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Dataflows Gen2 are a full replacement for a data warehouse in Microsoft Fabric.
content.back: False. Dataflows are explicitly not a replacement for a data warehouse — that's listed as a limitation. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-dataflow-gen-2-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? A Fabric capacity workspace is required to use Dataflows Gen2. ---
content.back: True. A Fabric capacity workspace is required to use Dataflows Gen2. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-dataflow-gen-2-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? A single pipeline can only contain one activity — Copy Data — and nothing else.
content.back: False. A pipeline can contain any combination of activities — data transformation and control flow — chosen to meet the specific need; Copy Data is common but not exclusive. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-data-factory-pipelines-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Pipeline runs can be triggered on-demand or scheduled to run at a specific frequency.
content.back: True. Runs can be started on-demand in the Fabric UI or scheduled to run at a specific frequency. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-data-factory-pipelines-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Pipeline templates in Microsoft Fabric are fixed and cannot be edited or customized after selection.
content.back: False. Templates are a starting point — you select one and then edit it in the pipeline canvas to customize it to your needs. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-data-factory-pipelines-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? The Copy Data activity supports a wide range of source connections, including lakehouse, warehouse, and SQL Database within OneLake. ---
content.back: True. In OneLake, Copy Data supports lakehouse, warehouse, SQL Database, and other destination/source types. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-data-factory-pipelines-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Deleting a managed table in the Spark catalog also deletes its underlying data.
content.back: True. Managed tables store their underlying data in the catalog's associated storage location; deleting the table deletes that data too. (External tables behave differently — deleting them removes only the metadata, not the underlying files.) (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-apache-spark-work-files-lakehouse/)

content.front: True or false? A temporary view created with createOrReplaceTempView persists permanently across all future Spark sessions.
content.back: False. A view is temporary — it's automatically deleted at the end of the current session, not persisted permanently. Persisted objects are tables, not views. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-apache-spark-work-files-lakehouse/)

content.front: True or false? Matplotlib can plot directly from a Spark dataframe without any conversion.
content.back: False. Matplotlib requires data in a Pandas dataframe, not a Spark dataframe — you need to call .toPandas() to convert it first before charting. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-apache-spark-work-files-lakehouse/)

content.front: True or false? Partitioning a saved dataframe (e.g., with partitionBy) can improve query performance by reducing unnecessary disk I/O when filtering. ---
content.back: True. Partitioning is explicitly called out as an optimization technique that reduces unnecessary disk I/O when queries filter on the partitioning column, improving performance across worker nodes. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/use-apache-spark-work-files-lakehouse/)

content.front: True or false? A stored function in KQL can accept parameters, allowing the same query logic to be reused with different values.
content.back: True. Functions can take parameters (e.g., trips_by_min_passenger_count(num_passengers:long)), letting you reuse the same logic with different input values. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/query-data-kql-database-microsoft-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Querying a materialized view always returns only the precomputed data as of the last background update, ignoring any newer data.
content.back: False. Materialized views combine the materialized part and the delta at query time, so they always return fresh, up-to-date results — not stale data frozen at the last background update. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/query-data-kql-database-microsoft-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? KQL databases can ingest data from sources like Azure Event Hubs, Fabric Eventstream, and Apache Kafka connectors.
content.back: True. The module explicitly lists Azure Event Hubs, Fabric Eventstream, Real-Time hub, and connectors including Apache Kafka among supported ingestion sources. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/query-data-kql-database-microsoft-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Reducing the number of columns selected (projecting early) has no effect on KQL query performance. ---
content.back: False. Projecting only needed columns early reduces resource usage and processing overhead — this is one of the module's explicit optimization techniques, especially valuable on wide tables. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/query-data-kql-database-microsoft-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Workspace-level roles (admin, contributor, member, viewer) apply to all items in a workspace, while item-level permissions allow more granular access control.
content.back: True. Workspace roles govern access at the whole-workspace level; item-level permissions layer on top for more granular, business-need-specific control. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/introduction-end-analytics-use-microsoft-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Copilot in Microsoft Fabric must be manually enabled by an administrator before any user can access it — it is disabled by default.
content.back: False. Copilot in Microsoft Fabric is enabled by default — administrators have the option to disable it (tenant-wide, by security group, or by capacity), not the other way around. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/introduction-end-analytics-use-microsoft-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ, and Work IQ are mutually exclusive — an organization can only use one at a time.
content.back: False. The three IQ workloads (Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ, Work IQ) are each standalone, but the module explicitly states they can be used together to provide comprehensive organizational context for agents — they aren't mutually exclusive. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/introduction-end-analytics-use-microsoft-fabric/)

content.front: True or false? The OneLake catalog only shows items that have been shared with the signed-in user. ---
content.back: True. The module states explicitly: in the OneLake catalog, you only see items that have been shared with you. (Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/introduction-end-analytics-use-microsoft-fabric/)
